title: Nilpotent natural fibre endomorphisms give a thick cohomology property
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be abelian categories, $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ an additive functor preserving finite limits and finite colimits, and $t:F\Rightarrow F$ a natural endomorphism. Suppose the ordinary derived category $D(\mathcal C)$ exists. Define $P(M)$ by the existence of $n\geq0$ with $t_M^n=0$. Then the class $Q$ of objects $K\in D(\mathcal C)$ such that $P(H^iK)$ holds for every integer $i$ is triangulated and stable under retracts, hence thick in the sense of [pur9-def-thick]. No boundedness or uniform exponent over the degrees is assumed.

source.place: Proof, Step 3: Nilpotent natural fibre endomorphisms give a thick cohomology property

proof.text: Naturality intertwines every power of t with F(f). Cancellation against a monomorphism or epimorphism shows that P passes to subobjects and quotients. The zero object has exponent one.

For a short exact sequence with nilpotence exponents a and b at its ends, exactness factors the b-th power on the middle fibre through the left fibre. Naturality then kills its composite with the a-th power. Thus a+b kills the middle fibre. These three closure properties make P a Serre property.

Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. Each cohomology object at the third vertex is an extension of a quotient and a subobject of adjacent cohomology objects at the other vertices. Shifts reindex the condition; zero has the condition. On a retract, each cohomology is a subobject of the corresponding cohomology of the ambient object, so P descends. This proves both clauses of thickness [pur9-def-thick]. The Lean proof uses the existing DerivedCategory.homologyProperty Serre-class API, with exactly these hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of the Kummer monodromy obstruction, preserving the flat-model and stratum-extension route.

theorem nilpotentFiberHomology_thick [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (t : F ⟶ F) :
    (nilpotentFiberHomology F t).IsTriangulated ∧
      (nilpotentFiberHomology F t).IsStableUnderRetracts
